verified: ReportURI said it identified 178 websites — Ars Technica names CNN, Zoom, the BBC and Salesforce as examples — serving JavaScript carrying a valid certificate for cdn.optimizely.com that had been modified to swap visitors' cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attackers', skim payment card data, steal cookies and screenshots, and deliver the Coruna and DarkSword iOS exploit kits (tool-2-1). Krebs on Security, citing ReportURI, reported that 68 of the affected sites had no Content Security Policy at all and only 24 (15 percent) had one that fully blocked the payload (tool-2-3).
unconfirmed: How the attackers wrote their code into each affected customer's snippet — the source says only that this happened "somehow" — and whether Optimizely's own systems were breached; the sources carry no attribution and no on-record Optimizely response, and the number of visitors actually infected is unknown. Reports also differ on details: Cointelegraph dates the injection to Monday and lists Ledger, BBC and IKEA among affected brands, while Ars Technica says researchers disclosed the finding Tuesday and names CNN, Zoom, the BBC and Salesforce (tool-2-2).

verified: ReportURI 称，其在 Optimizely 签发、经 cdn.optimizely.com 以有效证书分发的 JavaScript 中发现了被篡改的代码，共影响 178 个网站，包括 CNN、Zoom、BBC 和 Salesforce；恶意组件会替换加密货币钱包地址、窃取支付卡数据、Cookie 和截图，并在 iPhone/iPad 上投递 Coruna、DarkSword 漏洞利用套件（Ars Technica 引述该报告，Cointelegraph 亦有报道）。
unconfirmed: 上述发现目前仅来自 ReportURI 一家安全公司，尚未看到 Optimizely 的说明或第三方独立复现；攻击者具体如何把代码写入客户脚本、是否有访客数据被实际窃取、受影响站点是否已全部清除恶意代码，均未有交代。Cointelegraph 称攻击发生在周一，而 Ars 称研究人员周二披露，两篇报道在时间表述上并不一致。

titles.en: Malicious Optimizely-signed code hit 178 sites, stealing wallets and card data
titles.zh: Optimizely 签名脚本被篡改，178 家网站向访客投毒
